subject: The Other Side Village
comment: Hi City Council, We absolutely need to do something about the affordable housing crisis in our city. Please, vote in favor of The Other Side Village. Our city is covered in homeless camps. People are doing the best they can to survive and have a good life, but our city has become way too expensive. Once someone loses their home, it becomes very difficult to rebound financially. It's close to impossible to get and keep a job. With a housing first solution like this tiny home village, we can give some of these people the opportunity to regain financial and social power. I love that this village will provide a strong social network for its occupants. I don't like living in a city that is covered in homeless camps-not because it's an eye sore or because the people both me, but because I don't like what it indicates about the people who live in this city who DO have the power to change things. When I see these camps, or when I see my transient neighbors hanging out across the street, I'm reminded that I live in a city that is unwilling to question and stand up against the status quo. This is not the city I want to live in. Is this the city you want to live in? Thank you. Again, please vote in favor of The Other Side Village.
I would like to say that I think the OtherSide Village is great if somone wants to change there life and do something diffrent if the plan is followed

subject: The Other Side Village
comment: Hi City Council, I am writing to urge you to vote in favor of building The Other Side Village. Salt Lake City is in desperate need of real, long term solutions to our homelessness problem. Cities that undergo explosive economic and population growth like Salt Lake are always faced with an affordable housing problem. Homelessness is a result of a lack of affordable housing. Once a person loses housing, they are at risk for a number of problems. If we want our city to grow sustainably and be economically strong in the future, we must act now and work towards real solutions for affordable housing for everybody. I think that a lot of people see helping the homeless as a charitable act, done out of the goodness of their heart. I see it differently. I view creating strong social supports and affordable housing as a necessary economic action. A city in which the top 50% gets really rich and the bottom 50% becomes more desperate and unable to contribute to society is doomed to fail. Homelessness is a large and complex problem. It will not be solved completely with one tiny home village, I can acknowledge that. However, this is a great first step towards that solution. It will be a valuable additional to the arsenal our city currently has in ensuring each citizen gets their most basic needs met. Please vote in favor of The Other Side Village.

subject: Tiny Home Proposal in Glendale
comment: While I think we need more affordable house I worry that near the location of the Tiny Home village we'll have a lot of unsanctioned camps in the surrounding areas near the project. The 9-line is right there and I don't see how it'd be possible to keep encampments out of that area. I know that TOSA has said they would "patrol" which seems a little weird considering they aren't law enforcement but I have little to no faith that the city will do an adequate job not allow camps to form and grow. I believe this project will attract this to one of the only area's we don't have consistant camping. Also am suspicious of TOSA's programing. It has cultlike vibes to it that makes me really uncomfortable.

subject: gentrification
comment: Our neighborhood is already being gentrified. We don't need more gentrification. What we actually need is affordable low income housing to support the low income residents in the neighborhood. You also NEED to take into account the opinions of ALL Glendale/Poplar Grove residents (which comprise of Latinx & Tongan demographics). If you aim to help the community actually ask the community that lives there what they want. The white people on council, do not reflect nor represent the actual demographics of Glendale.

subject: The otherside village
comment: The village is an interesting idea, but should you put up an apartment building instead to house more individuals or make the little homes duplexes? Good luck.

subject: Other Side Village Comment
comment: Please reconsider siting this project at the current proposed location. The Westside neighborhoods Poplar Grove and Glendale suffer the consequences of high homeless populations enough as it is. The homeless persons are pushed from higher income neighborhoods to live on our streets. The homeless do need help but so do our neighborhoods. The Other Side Village isn't going to remove homeless from our parks and trails it will do nothing but increase the proliferation and lack of police effort to mitigate the homeless populations crimes. Unfortunately allowing and encouraging the homeless to run amok in neighborhoods like you are makes our neighborhoods dangerous. You are encouraging the spread of property and drug crime by putting up this village and using taxes to do it. When these people inevitably hurt me or my neighbors what recourse will we have to close this village. You are making an irreversible mistake that jeopardizes the improvement these neighborhoods have experienced. You are risking the potential for the North Temple transit corridor to be useable as well. No one will want to live and grow here if you continue to host all of the City's homeless into our neighborhoods. Mr. Puy please stand up for your neighborhoods and the home owners that are trying to raise safe families. Thank you.

subject: The Other Side
comment: Happy to see the proposal for The Other Side. Although I'd suggest something larger scale rather than single occupancy units. I think the city needs to develop more supportive housing in vacant areas away from the urban core. Downtown has suffered immensely from homeless expansion over the past 10 years. I moved out of downtown because the problems were so bad, and they still are. It's incredible that the city developed Magnolia over on 300 East, in an area where there are already so many no-income housing buildings, with most of their occupants being addicts and/or previously incarcerated persons. The city and state should think about developing other areas west of the city where there's ample and cheap land for supportive housing/shelters if they're going to put it anywhere. Still give people access to transportation via Trax. Get services on site and set up a system for healthcare providers to get tax breaks for providing services there. Taxpayer dollars are being allocated to put homeless and addicts in some of the most expensive real estate in the city which makes absolutely no sense.

subject: The Other Side Village
comment: Hi City Council, I am writing to ask you to vote in favor of building the Other Side Village. When I first heard about this idea, I was very excited about and told all my friends about it. A lot of people had already heard about it and were excited about it. The general consensus among my group of friends and family is that it is a great idea that won't immediately solve our growing homelessness problem, but it will definitely point us in the right direction. Please remember that the number one cause of homelessness is not affording a home. That seems obvious, but so often I hear people blaming addiction, laziness, disease, the economy, lack of education for the thousands of people across the state that don't have a place to live. If these people have an affordable and sustainable place to live with a strong social network, then they have solved their number one problem that caused their homelessness. Housed people have infinitely more opportunity to improve their lives and impact their community positively than the unhoused. Please consider voting in favor of the other side village.

subject: The Other Side Village
comment: I heard about this several months ago and I'm thrilled it is still under consideration. I appreciate that so much information is available about it, and having reviewed that information, I am even more excited at this possibility. The homeless situation, especially as it pertains to those individuals who are struggling with substance abuse and similar issues, is more visible in the Poplar Grove area than most places in the city, and this is a productive step in helping our neighbors get back on their feet. Thank you for considering this issue.

subject: Poplar Grove resident in support of The Other Side Village
comment: As a Poplar Grove resident, I voice my strong support for the Other Side Village project. After attending several events hosted by the leadership of the village project, I am more convinced than ever that the proposed community will be a boon to our neighborhood. Not only will this project bring needed amenities and gathering places that will benefit us all, but it will also represent an investment in human capital. While detractors of this project attempt to stoke fear of the problems that these new neighbors would bring to our community, let us instead focus on the amazing potential that this population will have more capacity to fulfill once they have a home. Meeting with past and current participants from the Other Side Academy emphasizes that every person can be an asset to their community when they are set up to succeed. The success of the Other Side Academy and its positive effects on its surrounding community give us every reason to believe in the capabilities of its leaders to realize their vision for this village. I urge the city council to accept the proposed lease of land for the Other Side Village. Let us be the neighborhood that benefits from welcoming this community.

subject: no gondola- please protect our land
comment: Hello, my name is Mia Mortensen. I grew up in Sandy at the base of little cottonwood canyon. And I'm emailing you today to PLEASE listen to your community and your environmental advocates that have spent years of their lives protecting the wasatch mountains. We are pleading for no gondola. This canyon deserves time for us as responsible citizens to explore options before destroying more land. Please do not let money blind you from the reality of this situation. There is TIME. Time to try other solutions first. We cannot go back from this.

subject: The Other Side Village
comment: Dear City Council, I'm writing to ask you to vote in favor of the Other Side Village. I would like to point out that this establishment is markedly different from "just another homeless shelter". Many people do not like homeless shelters built in their neighborhood because they are known to lower property values. However, The Other Side Village is not a homeless shelter. At a homeless shelter, visitors come in the evening, are assigned a bed, given some food, they might be connected with some social services, and then they leave in the morning. They spend their day trying to get by another day, and then repeat the process in the evening. The homeless shelter in no way is a home to these people; it is just a temporary shelter. Therefore, although each visitor in the shelter technically has a place to sleep for that one night, they are still without a home. In contrast, the Other Side Village is a community of homes. The people who will be living in this village will not just have temporary shelter, they will have homes-homes that they take care of, take pride in, clean, manage and decorate. They will have neighbors-neighbors that they will support and that will support them. They will have to pay rent for their home. They will be expected to live by community laws, and of course the laws of the city as a whole. It is easy to jump to conclusions and assume that this village will affect home values in the surrounding neighborhood the same way a homeless shelter would, but please take a moment to consider the significant differences between these two establishments. I expect that this neighborhood will have a very small affect on home values and crime rates in the neighborhood but will definitely have larger, very positive effects on the whole city. If you are on the fence about the Other Side Village, I ask you to please seriously consider the differences between this village and a homeless shelter. Thank you. Emma Scanlon

subject: The Other Side Village Support
comment: I wanted to express my support for the other side village rezoning and leasing of the property to the Other Side Village. The agency in question has constantly been willing to talk and answer my concerns. While I recognize the concerns for safety and health, I believe that providing our neighbors with a roof over their heads is the solution to homelessness. I strongly support the wrap around services, the community engagement. The success of previous Other Side programs also leads me to trust they will serve a community that needs it most. I ALSO encourage the city (and the county and the state) to find long term sustainable, integrated housing services for our homeless. Meet them where they are. Listen to what THEY need. Keep big business out of housing.

subject: Fleet Block Rezone
comment: Hi there! SLC needs a permanent food truck park. Building one in the Fleet Block would be a great way to support many small businesses at once. Especially if park/green space are included in the rezone. Thanks for considering!

subject: Tiny Home Village
comment: It's a complicated project on every level. I understand and empathize with residents who clearly want no part of the project. I am new. I haven't experienced the sense of abandonment and stigmatization my Westside neighbors have expressed. I, too, am discouraged by lack of investment in keeping parks safe and clean, camps by the river, broken down RVs in the neighborhood. However, I support the tiny home village. I supported it when it started, with 300 tiny homes. I saw the project succeed in Denver. I have observed housing models in Minneapolis and Duluth that have succeeded in providing stable housing to many of the most vulnerable citizens. I give our city council great praise for working hard to redesign the project to a reduced size and configuration. This is their diligent attempt to hear and respond to their constituents while supporting a much needed project. There are no easy answers to solving the social and economic problems that fuel our national crisis. The tiny Tiny Village is a start. I support it moving forward in our neighborhood. One concern is the requirement for strict sobriety. A model in Duluth allowed legal substance use in the privacy the the small studios. However, no residents were allowed only in the common space and no alcohol and drug use was allowed in these spaces. Perhaps there is a more reasonable solution for the concern about substance abuse. No one wants to be told what to do in their own home. Best wishes and thank you for your service. Deborah Esquibel Hunt, PhD

subject: The Other Side Village
comment: Hi SLC Council, I understand you will be discussing The Other Side Village today. I have a friend and former neighbor who is currently part of that program and it has been life changing for him. Before going into that program he had nowhere to go. He was down and constantly considering suicide. Now he has hope. I've never seen him happier nor have I seen him more productive. He has his confidence back and his zest for life. Please support this amazing program and help our brothers and sisters, our fellowmen/women, get back on their feet and not just survive, but succeed. Thanks, Jeromy Wilson
